channel.title: Polestar recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Polestar 3 Rear Seat Backrest Brackets May Be Loose
item.description: Some 2025 Polestar 3 vehicles have striker brackets that secure the rear seat backrest, and these brackets may be loose. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet federal safety rules for seating systems. If the brackets are loose, the rear seat backrest may not stay properly secured in place. A loose rear seat backrest may fall forward, allowing cargo behind the seat to enter the passenger area if the vehicle is in a crash.

item.title: Polestar 2 Rearview Camera May Not Display in Reverse
item.description: Certain 2021-2025 Polestar 2 vehicles may have a rearview camera image that does not display when the vehicle is placed in reverse. This recall replaces earlier recalls for this same issue, so vehicles that were already repaired under those earlier recalls will need to have the new repair performed. This means the driver may not get a picture of what's behind the vehicle when backing up, since the camera feed does not appear when the vehicle is placed in reverse.

item.title: Polestar 3 Front Bumper May Detach
item.description: Polestar is recalling certain 2025 Polestar 3 vehicles because the front hood wing bumper may be missing bolts. Without these bolts, the bumper could come loose and detach from the vehicle. Polestar will inspect the bumper for missing screws, and if any are missing, the bumper and screws will be replaced.

item.title: Polestar 3 Panoramic Sunroof Detachment Risk
item.description: On some 2025 Polestar 3 vehicles, the panoramic glass sunroof may not be properly secured and can detach from the vehicle.

item.title: Polestar 3 Wiring Damage May Cause Malfunctions
item.description: On certain Polestar 3 vehicles, water may damage the electrical connectors between the engine bay and front bumper cable harnesses. Damage to these harnesses can cause various electrical problems, such as a loss of power steering assist, which increases the risk of a crash or injury.

item.title: Polestar 2 May Lose Braking In One Pedal Drive
item.description: On affected vehicles, in certain driving situations — such as coasting down a hill while using the "One Pedal Drive" feature — the vehicle's brakes may stop working.

item.title: Polestar 3 Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: Polestar is recalling certain Polestar 3 vehicles because the rearview camera image may not display on the screen when the vehicle is placed in reverse. Because the image does not display, these vehicles do not meet a federal motor vehicle safety standard for rear visibility.

item.title: Polestar 2 back-up camera may not show an image
item.description: Polestar is recalling certain Polestar 2 vehicles. On these cars, the picture from the back-up camera may not appear when the vehicle is put into reverse. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule covering rear visibility. Dealers will update the vehicle software at no cost. Vehicles in this recall that were already repaired under an earlier recall, 24V-477, still need the new repair carried out.

item.title: Polestar 3 May Suddenly Lose Drive Power
item.description: On some Polestar 3 hybrid electric vehicles, changes in the 12-volt electrical system may damage a part called the High to Low Voltage Converter Module. A damaged module can cause the vehicle to suddenly lose drive power.

item.title: Polestar 2 Driver Airbag Clamps May Fail
item.description: On some Polestar 2 electric vehicles, the clamps on the driver's side inner far side airbag module may not be crimped correctly. This can cause that airbag to deploy the wrong way instead of working as intended.

item.title: Polestar 2 Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: On some Polestar 2 vehicles, a software problem in the infotainment head unit may prevent the rearview camera image from appearing on the screen. Without that camera image on the screen, the driver has less visibility behind the vehicle when backing up, which can make it harder to see what's behind the car. Polestar has released an over-the-air software update that fixes the issue. The update installs automatically and there is no cost to the owner.

item.title: Polestar 2 Recalled for Faulty Front Ball Joint
item.description: The front left lower ball joint on some vehicles may have been installed incorrectly. This could let the control arm disconnect from the steering knuckle, the part that connects the wheel to the steering system.

item.title: Polestar 2 Battery Software May Disconnect Power
item.description: In some Polestar 2 vehicles, the microprocessor in the Battery Energy Control Module can reset itself. When the microprocessor resets, it can cause the vehicle's high voltage system to disconnect. If the high voltage system disconnects, the vehicle can lose the power it needs to keep moving, resulting in a loss of drive power while the vehicle is being driven.
